candidates.title: Looping Deeper Without Growing the KV Cache: Recurrent Depth for Causal Encoder-Decoders
candidates.abstract: Looped language models deepen computation without adding parameters, yet caching full-context key-value (KV) states across layers and rounds severely bounds serving batch size. We design a looped causal encoder-decoder (CED) that achieves recurrent depth with zero round-wise KV growth, addressing where and how to loop an asymmetric stack in which only sparse encoder layers generate global KV. We find that recurrence must be placed in the encoder to iteratively refine global KV representations rather than re-reading static decoder projections, which both drives language-modeling gains and preserves long-context scaling. Furthermore, training the encoder loop under stochastic recurrence depth induces a fixed-point equilibrium where every round losslessly shares the last round's KV cache. Compounding cross-layer and cross-round KV sharing, the resulting Looped CED matches an unlooped CED's minimal memory footprint and recovers 86-93% of a looped Transformer's gain with 1/6 of its global KV. To test serving at production scale, we loop the 552B-parameter DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash for 8 rounds on one 4xGB200 node: with per-layer and per-round KV the loop cannot fit a single 128K-token request, whereas Looped CED holds 36.8x less KV per token, fits 38 such requests (as many as the unlooped model), and serves 3.6x higher throughput on 8K-token prompts.
candidates.reason: Designs a looped causal encoder-decoder whose encoder recurrence shares the last round KV cache losslessly, achieving zero round-wise KV growth and 1/6 of a looped transformer global KV, validated by looping the 552B DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash for serving.

candidates.title: EdgePrompt: A Distributed Key-Value Inference Framework for LLMs in 6G Networks
candidates.abstract: As sixth-generation (6G) networks advance, large language models (LLMs) are increasingly integrated into 6G infrastructure to enhance network management and intelligence. However, traditional LLMs architecture struggle to meet the stringent latency and security requirements of 6G, especially as the increasing in sequence length leads to greater task complexity. This paper proposes EdgePrompt, a cloud-edge collaborative framework based on a hierarchical attention splicing mechanism. EdgePrompt employs distributed key-value (KV) pair optimization techniques to accelerate inference and adapt to network conditions. Additionally, to reduce the risk of data leakage, EdgePrompt incorporates a privacy preserving strategy by isolating sensitive information during processing. Experiments on public dataset show that EdgePrompt effectively improves the inference throughput and reduces the latency, which provides a reliable solution for LLMs deployment in 6G environments.
candidates.reason: EdgePrompt is a cloud-edge collaborative framework using hierarchical attention splicing and distributed key-value pair optimization to raise LLM inference throughput and cut latency in 6G network deployments.

candidates.title: Task Offloading for Collaborative Inference of LLM Agents at the Network Edge
candidates.venue: IEEE International Conference on Mobile Adhoc and Sensor Systems
candidates.abstract: The deployment of large language models (LLMs) at the network edge has emerged as a critical paradigm for enabling low-latency, privacy-preserving AI services. However, resource-constrained user devices (e.g., smartphones, IoT endpoints) struggle to execute computationally intensive LLM inference tasks solely. Collaborative computing frameworks that offload subtasks to edge servers offer a promising solution but face challenges in balancing task completion latency, energy consumption, and dynamic network conditions. This paper addresses these challenges by proposing a two-stage optimization framework that jointly manages task offloading decisions and computational resource allocation, aiming to minimize the total task completion latency. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed algorithm reduces total latency by 49.6% compared to random, greedy, and genetic baselines, exhibits robust adaptability across varying energy budgets, and achieves 97.8% energy utilization in resource-constrained edge environments.
candidates.reason: Proposes a two-stage optimization of task offloading decisions and compute resource allocation for collaborative inference of LLM agents at the network edge, reducing total task completion latency by 49.6% versus random, greedy and genetic baselines.
